title: Playing backwards with J keeps up on a full-screen recording
goal: J plays a recording backwards, the way an editor shuttles back to find a spot. Forward playback was made fast on full-screen Retina recordings today, but backwards still reads one frame at a time the old way, so the picture probably sticks and jumps while the playhead runs. Measure it first, then make backward play keep up as forward play does. If the measure shows it already keeps up, say so in the log and close the task.
notes: Not yet reproduced: the step only plays forward (checkPlaybackNeverBlank in Sources/Photonz/Playtest/PlaytestHarness.swift ~9120 calls editor.playDocument from the start), so nobody has measured backward play. Source: audit 2026-10-07-retina-playback-keeps-up.json rough 2 ('Playing backwards (J) still reads frame by frame, the old slow way, so a full-screen recording played backwards can still lag') and commit 592bca7d ('frames across a cut and backward play still use the lanes', about 15 frames a second on this fixture). Forward fix: MoviePlayPass (Sources/PhotonzCore/MoviePlayPass.swift) plus Sources/Photonz/MovieFrames.swift. A backward pass could read a window of frames behind the playhead in one AVAssetReader pass and hand them out in reverse. Runs after a-full-screen-recording-keeps-up-as-it-plays-acr, which touches the same frame supply.
acceptance: The walk step that watches playback (expectPlaybackNeverBlank) can watch it play backwards (a direction or rate option), so it can be measured; PhotonzCore parse test first
Measured on Scripts/playtest/fixtures/Full screen Retina recording 3456x2234.mp4 at Next defaults: End, then J, watched 2.5 s at 20 looks. Before and after numbers in the log
After: no more than 2 looks late and none more than 2 frames behind, the same bar as forward play (PlaybackKeepsUp); J J (double speed back) stays smooth or degrades without going blank
A walk keeps it covered in the rotating check; Scripts/test.sh green; perf note in the commit
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: Adversarial review before building: Premiere and Final Cut users press End then J, then J J to go faster. On long-GOP footage they get a short pre-roll before reverse starts. Backwards plays silent here (playsSoundAtRate), so holding the clock briefly costs nothing in sound. No mock covers backward play; the transport is unchanged.

Harness bug found while measuring: expectPlaybackNeverBlank judged the shown frame with forward travel, but the canvas sets inHand.travel = playheadTravel (EditorState.swift:4697). Played backwards, it counted a frame from the far end as shown. Fixed: the step now sets travel the canvas way and its failure names the worst look (wanted frame, shown frame, time).

BEFORE (corrected step, Retina fixture, Next defaults, 2.5s at 20 looks): End then J 14/20 late, up to 17-18 frames; J J 15/20 late, up to 38 frames (2.0s). Forward 0/20. Cause: backward fetch read every frame through the 4 exact generator lanes, each seeking from the key frame (key frames at 0s and 2.0s, 60fps source).

AFTER: J 0/20 and J J 0/20 in 9 of 9 runs, plus 1 run under 4 CPU burners. Backwards across a cut 0/20 in 6 of 6 runs once the far side was read ahead (before that, 2 of 5 runs had the cut look 22 frames late). Block timings: 115-250ms per 10-12 frame block; the first block from rest about 215ms, which is the pre-roll.

Design: MoviePlayBackward (Sources/PhotonzCore/MoviePlayPass.swift). Blocks of 10 grid frames (20 at 2x) read in one AVAssetReader pass, lowest first, kept 10 frames (20 at 2x) behind the playhead. At most 2 per place and 3 per recording, and a block right behind the playhead reads alone. PhotonzDocument.moviePlayBackPlaces looks reach+block+1 steps back in time, so a stretch stops at a cut and the far side gets its own place. Pre-roll: EditorState.preRollBackward waits up to 500ms for readyToPlayBackward. Budget: 1+reach+block per place + 4; frames already shown (above the playhead) weigh 8x in eviction (MovieFrameQueue.backwardBehindWeight). App side: MovieFrameFetcher.playBack/openBack in Sources/Photonz/MovieFrames.swift.

Left rough, not filed: (1) J from rest holds the playhead about 0.2s (bounded at 0.5s). That is a deliberate choice and an evaluate question in the audit, not a defect. (2) 4x and 8x backwards read no further than 2x, to bound memory; not measured, and nobody has reported a problem. (3) A dissolve played backwards was not measured. Neither 2 nor 3 has a reproduction, so neither clears the follow-up bar.

J and J J now keep up on the full-screen Retina fixture, across a cut too (commit c4c0eb94). Backward play reads the stretch behind the playhead in one-pass blocks (MoviePlayBackward), opens the far side of a cut early, and waits about 0.2s from rest (at most 0.5s) for the frame behind. Before: J 14/20 looks late, up to 18 frames; J J 15/20, up to 38. After: 0/20 for both in 9 of 9 runs, also under load; across a cut 0/20 in 6 of 6. The step judges playback with the playhead's direction and takes a shuttle rate. playing-a-recording-backwards-keeps-up-walk covers it at Next defaults with real End/J/K keys. 10 neighbouring walks green, Scripts/test.sh green (11,825 tests).
